resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection (CI) for sale
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Neptune City Zoning and Code Enforcement (Code Official)
resale_co.lead_time: At least five business days notice is required to schedule the inspection; the inspector sets the date and time.
requirements: Interior and exterior property maintenance inspection by the Code Official (walks, exterior, steps, house numbers at least 3 inches, kitchen, bathrooms, basement, occupancy limits)
Smoke detector on every story including the basement, and outside of and within 10 feet of every bedroom; carbon monoxide detectors where required (check with the official)
All open construction permits must be finalized before the CI is issued for a dwelling being sold
Stove anti-tip bracket, dryer vented outside with rigid pipe, door between house and attached garage
Megan's Law statement signed by the new owner
An adult reachable at the phone number on the application to confirm the inspection time

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Borough's Certificate of Inspection application (check Sale), list the new occupants, and submit it with the $120.00 fee by check payable to Borough of Neptune City at Borough Hall, 106 West Sylvania Avenue. Call 732-776-9204 x 35 to arrange the inspection, with at least five business days notice. Close any open construction permits first.

resale_co.notes: Borough Code Section 102-15 requires a Certificate of Inspection from the Code Official before any building is sold and occupied. The Borough's Master Fee Schedule (Resolution 2026-74, adopted March 23, 2026) and the April 2026 application both set the CI fee at $120 per unit, with $200 for a reinspection after a failed inspection and $60 for an updated certificate. The ecode360 copy of Section 62-6 still shows the older fees ($60 inspection, $35 reinspection, $20 update); Ordinance 2026-01 moved these fees into the Master Fee Schedule, so the $120 figure is the current one. The Zoning and Code Enforcement page lists Frank Cinelli (Code Enforcement Officer, code@neptunecitynj.com) and Chris Willms (Zoning Officer, firemarshal@neptunecitynj.com). The Borough website blocks automated readers; the application link may need to be opened in a browser. Section 62-6 also mentions a landlord registration form and lead inspection payment for pre-1978 structures; these apply to rentals, not owner-occupied sales. Ecode360 also lists a separate $20 certificate of continued occupancy fee under Section 62-6(C); the CI is the document the Borough asks for on sales.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area (N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19); the Borough CI checklist also asks for a smoke detector on every story including the basement and within 10 feet of every bedroom
Carbon monoxide alarm near the sleeping areas in homes with fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Battery-only smoke alarms should be 10-year sealed units; hardwired alarms may not be replaced with battery-only units (state rule)

authorities.name: Neptune City Bureau of Fire Prevention (Borough Fire Marshal)
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate Borough smoke/CO certificate application or fee schedule was found online. The Borough's Certificate of Inspection checks smoke and CO detectors. Contact the Fire Marshal at firemarshal@neptunecitynj.com or 732-580-2128 to confirm whether a separate smoke/CO certificate is issued for sales.

fire_cert.notes: Neptune City is a fire department LEA (code F) and Borough Code Chapter 64 names the Bureau of Fire Prevention as the local enforcing agency. No Borough page, form or ordinance section setting a smoke/CO certificate (CSACMAPFEC) fee was found; Chapter 64 lists only commercial and multi-family inspection fees. The CI inspection checks smoke and CO detectors, but it is not clear whether the Fire Marshal also issues a separate state-format smoke/CO certificate for sales. The state directory lists the smoke detector compliance office as Neptune City Borough Construction at 106 W Sylvania Ave, (732) 776-7224. The CI checklist does not list a fire extinguisher, consistent with the February 2025 state change (P.L.2025, c.19).

open_questions: Does the Fire Marshal issue a separate smoke/CO certificate (CSACMAPFEC) for sales, and if so what is the fee, or does the $120 Certificate of Inspection cover it?
How long is a Certificate of Inspection valid before closing?
Is the $20 certificate of continued occupancy (Section 62-6(C)) ever required in addition to the CI on a sale?
